title: Haeckel correspondence: preparation manufacture, specimen shipment, professional sale, and radiolarian slide gift

principal_upgrade.previous_state: A-level digital-correspondence comparator with one known 1896 Radiolaria glass-slide gift
principal_upgrade.new_state: A bounded search of the official Ernst Haeckel Online Briefedition now yields four distinct material/circulation mechanisms: amateur preparation manufacture for social viewing (1852), expedition specimens shipped from the Challenger Office to Haeckel for taxonomic/reporting work with railway-expense paperwork (1880), professional prepared specimens sent on approval and offered for purchase with item prices (1885), and a Radiolaria collection sent outward by Haeckel as a gift of glass slides for microscopic viewing (1896).

grade.digital_primary_source_authority: S — official Friedrich Schiller University Jena critical online correspondence edition with TEI, metadata, shelfmarks and citation data
grade.whole_correspondence_corpus_exhaustivene: A+/open — current pass is a bounded keyword harvest, not a complete TEI export of all preparation-related letters
grade.surviving_object_crosswalk: open — the letters establish transaction/material movement, but present-day survival of the exact shipped/gifted preparations is not claimed

edition_authority.scope_statement: The project aims to make the complete surviving correspondence of Haeckel, including letters and counter-letters, searchable in full text, with critical transcription and metadata.

object_or_practice: potato preparation for viewing starch grains, stained with iodine tincture
microscope taken to an evening gathering at the sender's brother's house
promise to bring the microscope again at Pentecost and make new preparations
request to Haeckel for interesting and readily obtainable material, including preservable infusoria
events.interpretive_value: Preparation-making appears as a repeatable social obligation generated by successful microscopic demonstration, not only as a research-laboratory task.

shipment.origin_context: recent sea trip north of Scotland

events.research_task: Murray asks Haeckel to identify the genera of Radiolaria in surface gatherings for a preliminary report being prepared by Wyville Thomson; he also asks questions about spicules in the mud and the Actinia.
events.prior_route: Murray explicitly recalls having sent Haeckel Actinia from the Challenger earlier and asks whether he examined them or could delegate them to a pupil for a report.
events.administrative_layer: The same letter asks Haeckel to produce a railway bill/copy or a rewritten note because Treasury officials require accounts or an approved form for payment documentation.
events.interpretive_value: Specimen circulation, expert labour, publication/reporting and reimbursement paperwork occur in a single correspondence event. The material route is therefore simultaneously scientific and administrative.

events.transaction: Wiese sends preparations for inspection and possible purchase after noting that Haeckel had accepted skeletons from him about four years earlier.
events.guard: The listed preparations are principally skeleton/zoological preparations; do not recode the entire letter as microscope-slide commerce. Its value is as a preparator-market comparator inside Haeckel's material network.

events.prior_action: Haeckel had sent delle Grazie a valuable package including his portrait and a Radiolaria collection.
events.recipient_description: Delle Grazie calls the Radiolaria collection a great gift and anticipates viewing the small glass slides (Glastäfelchen) under the microscope.
events.interpretive_value: Prepared microscopic objects moved outward from Haeckel's scientific world as a gift whose value depended on later microscopic viewing by the recipient.

mechanism.statement: The Haeckel correspondence is useful less as a single provenance chain than as a transaction grammar. The same category 'preparation' moves through amateur making, expedition logistics, paid preparator commerce, expert report production and gift exchange.
mechanism.comparison_with_cabinets: Cole and Gibson preserve material relations spatially in cabinets. Haeckel's correspondence preserves relations temporally as actions: send, inspect, buy, return, identify, report, reimburse, give and view.

guards: The bounded keyword harvest is not an exhaustive corpus export.
The 1885 Wiese material is mostly macroscopic prepared skeletons; retain it as a professional preparator-market comparator, not as direct slide evidence.
The 1896 letter proves delivery and intended microscopic viewing of a Radiolaria glass-slide collection but does not by itself identify the source specimens, slide maker or present survival.
The 1880 North-of-Scotland shipment and earlier Challenger Actinia should not be merged unless a separate letter or register closes the relation.

exact_next_actions.action: Harvest the John Murray/Challenger correspondence around 1876-1888 for box, bottle, mud, Radiolaria, Actinia, railway, freight, account and report terms; preserve each shipment as a dated event.
Search outward Haeckel letters for Radiolariencollection/Glastäfelchen/Präparate Geschenk to identify other gift recipients and whether any set numbering or slide-maker language appears.
Search professional preparator correspondence for approval-sale language (zur Ansicht, Ankauf, Preis, zurück) and separate microscopic mounts from anatomical/skeletal preparations.

stop_rule: Do not broaden into Haeckel biography. Continue only with correspondence queries that add a new transaction type, close a shipment to a publication/report, or identify surviving preparations.
